content: Concurrent use of magnesium hydroxide with calcium, aluminum, or iron significantly reduces plasma levels of magnesium hydroxide. No human studies have been conducted to confirm this interaction. Bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens may decrease magnesium hydroxide levels by shifting magnesium from the blood to tissue storage. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Bendroflumethiazide reduces magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of bictegravir through cation binding in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract. Bictegravir should be taken under fasting conditions at least 2 hours before or 2 hours after antacids containing aluminum, magnesium, or calcium. Routine simultaneous administration is not recommended. Bumetanide decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the levels or effects of cabotegravir by cation binding in the GI tract. Antacids should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after oral cabotegravir. Calcitonin salmon increases magnesium hydroxide levels by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the levels or effects of chloroquine by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Doses should be separated by at least 4 hours. Chlorothiazide decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Chlorthalidone decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Magnesium hydroxide reduces ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Co-administration with multivalent cation-containing products may reduce ciprofloxacin bioavailability by up to 90%. Ciprofloxacin should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after these products. Conjugated estrogens decrease magnesium hydroxide levels by shifting magnesium from the blood to tissue storage. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Vaginal conjugated estrogens also decrease magnesium hydroxide levels by shifting magnesium from the blood to tissue storage. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Magnesium hydroxide decreases crizotinib levels by increasing gastric pH. Drugs that elevate gastric pH may reduce crizotinib solubility and bioavailability. No formal studies have been conducted to confirm this interaction. Cyclopenthiazide decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Magnesium hydroxide reduces deferiprone levels by enhancing GI absorption. Deferiprone may bind polyvalent cations such as iron, aluminum, and zinc. Administration should be separated by at least 4 hours between deferiprone and other medications or supplements containing these cations. Magnesium hydroxide and deflazacort both decrease serum potassium levels. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Magnesium hydroxide reduces demeclocycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Alternative drugs should be considered. Dextrose decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Digoxin decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Magnesium hydroxide reduces dolutegravir levels or effects by cation binding in the GI tract. Dolutegravir should be administered 2 hours before or 6 hours after medications containing polyvalent cations. Alternative therapies should be considered if available. Doxercalciferol increases magnesium hydroxide levels by enhancing GI absorption. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Magnesium hydroxide reduces doxycycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Alternative drugs should be considered. Drospirenone increases magnesium hydroxide levels by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Magnesium hydroxide reduces eltrombopag levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Co-administration is contraindicated, and doses should be separated by at least 4 hours. Estradiol decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by shifting magnesium from the blood to tissue storage. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Synthetic conjugated estrogens decrease magnesium hydroxide levels by shifting magnesium from the blood to tissue storage. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Estropipate decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by shifting magnesium from the blood to tissue storage. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Ethacrynic acid decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Magnesium hydroxide reduces fleroxacin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Doses should be separated by 2 hours. Furosemide decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Magnesium hydroxide reduces gemifloxacin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Doses should be separated by 2 hours. Gentamicin decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Intranasal glucagon increases magnesium hydroxide levels by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Hydrochlorothiazide decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Magnesium hydroxide reduces ibandronate levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Indapamide decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the levels or effects of infigratinib by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. If co-administration with an acid-reducing agent cannot be avoided, infigratinib should be administered 2 hours before and after a locally-acting antacid. Lanthanum carbonate and magnesium hydroxide may interact through cation binding in the GI tract. Antacids should be administered at least 2 hours before or after lanthanum. Magnesium hydroxide reduces levofloxacin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Doses should be separated by 2 hours. Mannitol decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Magnesium hydroxide reduces moxifloxacin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Doses should be separated by 2 hours. Neomycin decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Magnesium hydroxide reduces nitrofurantoin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Magnesium hydroxide reduces ofloxacin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Doses should be separated by 2 hours. Magnesium hydroxide reduces omadacycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Multivalent cation-containing products may impair absorption of tetracyclines, reducing their efficacy. Dosing should be separated. Magnesium hydroxide reduces oxytetracycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Alternative drugs should be considered. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the effects of pancrelipase through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Antacids may negate the beneficial effects of enzymes. Paromomycin decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Magnesium hydroxide reduces pazopanib levels by increasing gastric pH. Co-administration with drugs that raise gastric pH should be avoided. Short-acting antacids may be used instead of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) and H2 antagonists, but antacid and pazopanib dosing should be separated by several hours. Magnesium hydroxide reduces penicillamine levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Doses should be separated by 2 hours. Magnesium hydroxide reduces pexidartinib levels or effects by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Doses should be separated by 2 hours before or after taking a locally-acting antacid. Magnesium hydroxide reduces ponatinib levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Alternative drugs should be considered. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the effects of potassium phosphates (IV) through cation binding in the GI tract. Magnesium decreases serum phosphate concentration by binding dietary phosphate. Alternative drugs should be considered. Magnesium hydroxide reduces raltegravir levels or effects by cation binding in the GI tract. Magnesium-containing antacids reduce raltegravir plasma levels when taken within 6 hours of the raltegravir dose. Magnesium hydroxide reduces riociguat levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Doses should be separated by at least 1 hour. Magnesium hydroxide reduces sarecycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Multivalent cation-containing products may impair absorption of tetracyclines, reducing their efficacy. Dosing should be separated. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the effects of sodium phosphates (IV) through cation binding in the GI tract. Magnesium decreases serum phosphate concentration by binding dietary phosphate. Alternative drugs should be considered. Sodium polystyrene sulfonate increases magnesium hydroxide levels by decreasing renal clearance. There is a risk of alkalosis. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Magnesium hydroxide reduces sotorasib levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. If co-administration with an acid-reducing agent cannot be avoided, sotorasib should be administered 4 hours before or 10 hours after a locally-acting antacid. Spironolactone increases magnesium hydroxide levels by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Streptomycin decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Magnesium hydroxide reduces tetracycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Alternative drugs should be considered. Tobramycin decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Triamterene increases magnesium hydroxide levels by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Magnesium hydroxide reduces vismodegib levels or effects by altering gastric pH, which affects solubility and bioavailability. The effect on efficacy is unknown. Vitamin D increases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing serum magnesium concentrations, particularly in the presence of renal impairment. Combined use of vitamin D and magnesium-containing products should be avoided in patients with chronic renal failure. Adverse effects of magnesium hydroxide include abdominal cramping, diarrhea, electrolyte imbalance, hypotension, muscle weakness, respiratory depression, renal failure, myocardial damage, heart block, fecal impaction, rectal fissures, intestinal obstruction, and undiagnosed abdominal pain. Use with caution in renal insufficiency. It is generally considered safe during pregnancy (Category A) and lactation.
